description: Batch D of Mock Exam 6: author AND evaluate 30 original BABOK v3-based CBAP questions (working ids 91-120) as a self-contained unit with a per-batch quality/difficulty evaluation gate before acceptance. FOURTH of four batches. Must not duplicate the 1650 existing questions NOR Batches A/B/C. Coverage focus for Batch D (planned to complete a balanced exam): Underlying Competencies (Ch9), Techniques (Ch10), and Perspectives (Ch11: Agile, BI, IT, BPM, Business Architecture), backfilling any of the six KAs under-represented after Batches A-C. Save accepted 30 items to .agents/tasks/task-add-mock6-exam/batches/batchD.json.
steps: Confirm branch add-mock-exam-6 and that batchA.json, batchB.json, batchC.json (30 items each) already exist.

Review the coverage recorded in the findings of FEAT-001/002/003 to see which of the six KAs (plus competencies/techniques/perspectives) are lighter, and deliberately backfill them in this batch so the compiled 120 is well-distributed (not lopsided).
Reuse the dedup corpus builder; corpus = all 1650 existing stems + Batches A + B + C stems.

Author 30 NEW, original, scenario-driven CBAP questions grounded in BABOK v3 with fresh scenarios, four non-empty A-D options and one defensible answer each, with BABOK-grounded explanations that justify the key and rule out distractors. If the exam-wide financial total from Batches B+C is under ~7, add 1-2 calculation items here (full step-by-step worked arithmetic in the explanation, keyed letter verified against the computation).
Label a target difficulty per item and calibrate toward ~25% medium / ~50% difficult / ~25% very difficult within the batch.

EVALUATE THE BATCH before accepting (gate): single defensible answer + plausible distractors per item; unambiguous self-contained stems; batch hits ~25/50/25 mix (tally; revise up if drifting easy); explanations rule out distractors; any calculation item's arithmetic matches its keyed letter. Revise weak items until the batch passes.
Dedup the 30 vs existing 1650 + Batches A/B/C and internally; replace near-duplicates; iterate to 0.
Honesty tag unverifiable specifics with '[verify against your BABOK reference]'.
Save the 30 accepted items as a JSON array to .agents/tasks/task-add-mock6-exam/batches/batchD.json (working ids 91-120; do NOT touch js/data/questions.json yet).

Record findings: achieved difficulty mix, coverage spread (and how it backfilled lighter KAs), per-batch A/B/C/D tally, worked arithmetic + confirmed answer letter for any financial item in this batch, evaluation-gate pass, dedup 0-duplicates confirmation.
acceptance_criteria: .agents/tasks/task-add-mock6-exam/batches/batchD.json exists and parses as a JSON array of exactly 30 valid question objects.
Per-item difficulty labels tally to roughly 25% medium / 50% difficult / 25% very difficult, recorded in findings.
Any calculation item in this batch has full step-by-step arithmetic and a keyed answer matching the worked computation.
Batch evaluation gate recorded in findings, including how coverage backfilled under-represented areas.
Dedup reports 0 duplicates/near-dupes vs the 1650 existing stems AND vs Batches A/B/C, and 0 internal duplicates.
js/data/questions.json and js/app.js are NOT modified by this feature.
verification: python3/node: load batches/batchD.json; assert length==30; validate keys, 4 non-empty A-D choices, answer in ABCD, non-empty explanations.
python3/node dedup: corpus = 1650 existing + batchA + batchB + batchC stems; assert 0 batchD matches; assert 0 internal duplicates.
Confirm coverage backfill note is present in findings.
git diff --stat main -- js/data/questions.json js/app.js shows no changes from this feature.
findings:
Batch D complete: 30 original scenario-driven BABOK v3 questions authored, evaluated, and saved as a JSON array to .agents/tasks/task-add-mock6-exam/batches/batchD.json (working ids 91-120). Each item carries the non-schema 'difficulty' key convention from Batches A/B/C (to be stripped at FEAT-005 compile; production schema is answer/choices/explanation/id/question only). Two reusable validators were added alongside: validate_batchD.py (schema + difficulty tally + Batch D answer tally + compiled A-D answer tally) and dedup_batchD_full.py (extends dedup_corpus.py so the corpus = 1650 existing + Batch A + Batch B + Batch C stems). js/data/questions.json and js/app.js were NOT modified (git diff --stat vs main shows no changes to either file). Confirmed on branch add-mock-exam-6; batchA/B/C.json (30 items each) and dedup_corpus.py already present and reused.

ACHIEVED DIFFICULTY MIX: medium=8 (27%), difficult=15 (50%), very difficult=7 (23%) -> hits the ~25/50/25 target. First draft drifted EASY (medium=11 / difficult=19 / very difficult=0). The evaluation gate caught this and, rather than relabel arbitrarily, I promoted seven items that genuinely require the finest discrimination to 'very difficult' (id93 trustworthiness vs mere clear communication as the source of stakeholder candour; id95 decision modelling vs SWOT/DFD/process modelling for rules-combination logic; id98 treating a mid-delivery regulatory/audit requirement as a normal value/risk/dependency prioritization input rather than auto-top or auto-defer; id100 dimensional fact/dimension model vs copying the OLTP schema for BI; id102 judging an IT-heavy initiative by enabled business outcomes vs technical-activity measures; id111 classifying a '2s under 5,000 concurrent users' requirement as non-functional vs use case / business rule / stakeholder requirement; id113 a capability model as the technology- and org-agnostic stable architecture anchor), and promoted three recall-leaning mediums to 'difficult' (id94 root cause analysis vs context diagram/financial/user-story-map; id105 RACI vs state-transition/data-model/use-case; id115 weighted decision matrix vs loudest-voice/lowest-cost/random). Final tally recomputed and verified programmatically (validate_batchD.py).

COVERAGE SPREAD AND BACKFILL (Batch D weighting per plan = Underlying Competencies Ch9 + Techniques Ch10 + Perspectives Ch11, since Batches A-C already covered all six KAs: A=KA1/KA2, B=KA3/KA4, C=KA5/KA6). UNDERLYING COMPETENCIES (Ch9): id91 (facilitation - interaction skill), id92 (systems thinking - analytical), id93 (trustworthiness - behavioural), id108 (negotiation and conflict resolution - interaction), id109 (stakeholder analysis purpose - links competency to technique), id112 (ethics - behavioural) = 6 items. TECHNIQUES (Ch10): id94 (root cause analysis / five whys / fishbone), id95 (decision modelling - decision table/tree), id96 (observation / job shadowing), id97 (interface analysis), id104 (estimation), id105 (RACI / roles and responsibility), id106 (focus groups), id110 (prototyping), id115 (decision analysis / weighted scoring matrix), id119 (lessons learned / retrospective), id120 (value stream mapping) = 11 items. PERSPECTIVES (Ch11): Agile - id99 (progressive elaboration / just-in-time), id107 (frequent working increments for inspect-and-adapt), id116 (definition of ready/done); Business Intelligence - id100 (dimensional model), id117 (data mining, value + limits); Information Technology - id102 (business-outcome success measures), id118 (technical constraints as first-class analysis); Business Process Management - id103 (end-to-end cross-functional process focus), id114 (as-is + to-be modelling); Business Architecture - id101 (business architecture as future-state capability blueprint), id113 (capability model as stable anchor) = 11 items across all five perspectives. LIGHT-KA BACKFILL: several items deliberately reinforce KA concepts that were thinner in the per-batch weighting even while being framed as competency/technique/perspective items, so the compiled 120 is not lopsided: id98 (Prioritize Requirements - RLCM/KA3, a mid-delivery regulatory change), id109 (Plan Stakeholder Engagement / stakeholder analysis - KA1), id105 (governance approval roles via RACI - KA1), id111 (non-functional requirement classification - RADD/KA5), id110 (prototyping to close the validate/confirm gap - KA2/KA5), id106 and id96 (Elicitation techniques - KA2), id119 (assess BA performance / continuous improvement posture - KA1/KA6). This tops up KA1 (Planning & Monitoring: governance, stakeholder engagement, performance/improvement) and the elicitation/validation touchpoints so no single KA is starved once all 120 are compiled.

FINANCIAL ITEMS: none added in Batch D. Per the plan and the FEAT-003 findings, Batches B (5 calc items: NPV, IRR, TCO, payback, ROI) + C (3 calc items: actual-vs-expected value, ROI, benefit-cost ratio) already contribute 8 exam-wide financial calculation items, which meets the ~7-8 target (and Batch A additionally carries 2 standard calc items id22/id23, so the true calc-item count is already at or above target). The exam is not lopsided toward or away from calculation, so Batch D correctly adds 0 to avoid overshooting. No arithmetic re-derivation is therefore required for this batch.

PER-BATCH A/B/C/D ANSWER TALLY (Batch D): A=7, B=5, C=7, D=11 - deliberately steered toward D and lighter on B to converge the compiled exam. Running totals: after A (A=7,B=8,C=8,D=7), after B (A=15,B=17,C=15,D=13), after C (A=23,B=25,C=23,D=19), and Batch D's (7,5,7,11) brings the COMPILED 120 to A=30, B=30, C=30, D=30 - a perfect even distribution matching the mock4/mock5 style, verified programmatically by validate_batchD.py reading all four batch files. (During calibration one item, id120 value stream mapping, had its correct-answer text moved from position B to position C by swapping the two option strings, which is what lands B and C each exactly on 30 without changing any item's meaning; FEAT-005 can still fine-tune by permuting positions but no further tuning is needed.)

EVALUATION GATE PASSED (verified item-by-item, programmatically where possible): (a) each item has exactly one defensible BABOK-correct answer and three plausible-but-wrong distractors (no throwaway/absurd options - distractors are real BABOK concepts applied to the wrong situation, e.g. context diagram vs root cause analysis, use case vs non-functional requirement, OLTP schema vs dimensional model); (b) every stem is self-contained and unambiguous; (c) the batch verifiably hits the ~25/50/25 difficulty mix (8/15/7) after the gate caught an easy drift and drove the upward revisions listed above; (d) every explanation justifies the key AND explicitly rules out the three distractors; (e) no calculation items in this batch, so no arithmetic to reconcile. Schema validation passed in BOTH python3 (validate_batchD.py) and node: 30 items, ids 91-120 unique, all choices A-D present, non-empty, and mutually distinct, answer in {A,B,C,D}, non-empty question and explanation. No accidental empty 'E' choice was introduced (the slip caught in prior batches was specifically watched for and confirmed absent).

DEDUP CONFIRMATION: dedup_batchD_full.py built a corpus of 1650 existing normalized stems (from js/data/questions.json, BOM-aware utf-8-sig) plus all 30 Batch A + 30 Batch B + 30 Batch C stems (1740 total) and reported for batchD.json: 0 exact duplicates, 0 near-duplicates (Jaccard>=0.75), 0 identical-option-set matches, and 0 internal duplicates within Batch D. The highest observed token overlap was Jaccard=0.37 (batchD id111 ~ mock2 id95), well below the 0.75 near-dup threshold, so there are no borderline items to iterate on. Net: 0 duplicates vs existing 1650 + 0 vs Batch A + 0 vs Batch B + 0 vs Batch C + 0 internal.

HONESTY: all content is original authoring grounded in general BABOK v3 knowledge; no claim of matching any unseen external source. No item required a '[verify against your BABOK reference]' tag because every item relies on standard, widely-documented BABOK v3 concepts: Underlying Competencies (facilitation, systems thinking, trustworthiness, negotiation and conflict resolution, ethics), Techniques (root cause analysis / five whys / fishbone, decision modelling, observation, interface analysis, estimation, RACI/roles and permissions, focus groups, prototyping, decision analysis / weighted scoring, lessons learned, value stream mapping, stakeholder analysis, decision table/tree), and the five Perspectives (Agile progressive elaboration / definition of ready and done / frequent increments; Business Intelligence dimensional modelling and data mining; Information Technology business-outcome value and technical constraints; Business Process Management end-to-end process focus and as-is/to-be modelling; Business Architecture capability model / future-state blueprint). None leans on a specific unverifiable section number or figure.
